exposure: Annual average fine particulate matter (PM2.5) level at maternal residence
Annual average nitrogen dioxide (NO2) level at maternal residence
cohort: 285,594 singleton pregnancies in Victoria, Australia, occurring between March 1, 2012, and December 31, 2015
finding: An interquartile range increase in annual average NO2 exposure was associated with a reduced likelihood of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, GDM, and placental abruption, while findings for PM2.5 exposure were mixed and require further investigation.
